answer: Trust propagates from a verified beacon through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with degree-normalized transitions, so repeated identities do not create independent trust. A sybil cluster connected to honest users by a sparse cut has low conductance; over t steps, incoming walk mass is bounded by seed mass times t and the cut-to-volume ratio. Thus min-cut/transitivity limits aggregate voting weight. A plume of aliases or timber-themed accounts adds none without attestations.
